name: Ariane 64 Block 2 (4x P160C, Vulcain 2.1, Vinci) — TIMELINE mode

stages.name: P160C

propellant_kg.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P160C (155,600 kg; also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariane_6 Block 2 booster table)

dry_kg.derived: Wikipedia P160C gross mass 167,000 kg minus propellant mass 155,600 kg (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P160C)

thrust_vac_N.derived: Average thrust so the published load is consumed in the published burn: 155600 kg * 278.5 s * 9.80665 m/s^2 / 137 s = 3,101,951 N. Wikipedia's 4,780 kN is the maximum, not this average; using the maximum at Isp 278.5 s would burn far more than 155.6 t in 137 s. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P160C

thrust_sl_N.assumption: Sea-level thrust of the P160C is not published separately from the 4,780 kN maximum. The constant-thrust model uses the same average for SL and vacuum, so nozzle atmospheric loss is not modelled.

cutoff_s.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P160C burn time 137 s. ESA VA271 publishes booster separation at T+2:23 (143 s), not burnout; separation is a launch override.

stages.note: TIMELINE: constant average thrust. Four boosters in parallel with the LLPM from T0.

propellant_kg.src: https://cnes.fr/projets/ariane-6/modeles (LLPM '150 tonnes' of LOX/LH2). Wikipedia's infobox says 140,000 kg and eoPortal 140,000 kg; those do not close with 1,370 kN at 432 s over the 465 s VA271 MECO (that product is 150,373 kg). CNES 150 t is the figure used.

thrust_vac_N.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariane_6 (Vulcain 2.1 maximum thrust 1,370 kN). eoPortal quotes 1,371 kN vacuum.

thrust_sl_N.derived: CNES 'poussée au décollage de 135 tonnes' for Vulcain 2.1: 135 * 9.80665e3 = 1,323,898 N. https://cnes.fr/projets/ariane-6/modeles

ignition_s.src: https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/space-transportation/ariane/watch-live-ariane-6-launches-another-set-of-amazon-leo-satellites-to-orbit core burns from liftoff; MECO is T+7:45 on VA271

cutoff_s.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariane_6 LLPM burn time 468 s (generic). VA271 MECO T+7:45 (465 s) is a launch override.

propellant_kg.src: https://www.esa.int/fr/articles/about-us/directorates/space-transportation/ariane/ariane-6-what-s-it-made-of (upper stage 'fuelled by 30 tonnes'). Wikipedia infobox says 32,000 kg; eoPortal 31,000 kg. 30 t covers the VA271 burns (about 24.5 t at 180 kN / 457.2 s) with residual for the APU and deorbit.

thrust_sl_N.assumption: Vinci ignites after core separation, above the atmosphere. Sea-level thrust is not used; set equal to vacuum so Ae is 0.

ignition_s.src: https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/space-transportation/ariane/watch-live-ariane-6-launches-another-set-of-amazon-leo-satellites-to-orbit VA271 first Vinci ignition T+7:59. Generic ignition is not published; this is the VA271 time and launches may override it.

cutoff_s.src: https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/space-transportation/ariane/watch-live-ariane-6-launches-another-set-of-amazon-leo-satellites-to-orbit VA271 first Vinci cutoff T+17:51. The second burn is post-cutoff, not this cutoff.

mass_kg.assumption: Beyond Gravity says Ariane 6 fairings weigh 1.8 to 2.6 t and describes them as up to 20 m and 1,800 kg light (https://www.beyondgravity.com/en/news/shaping-next-generation-european-launch-vehicles-contract-won-ariane-6). The source does not assign which end of the range is the 20 m shell. Amazon Leo uses the long 20 m fairing (Wikipedia: Ariane 6). The 20 m shell is ASSUMED to be 2,600 kg, the top of that range.

header_notes: Ariane 64 Block 2. P160C propellant, gross mass, Isp and 137 s burn from Wikipedia P160C. Constant thrust is the average that consumes that load, not the 4,780 kN maximum.

LLPM propellant 150 t from CNES (Wikipedia 140 t does not close with 1,370 kN at 432 s over a 465 s MECO). Dry mass 23 t from ESA. Vulcain vacuum thrust 1,370 kN (Wikipedia) and 432 s (eoPortal). Sea-level thrust 135 tonnes-force (CNES).
ULPM 30 t / Vinci 180 kN / 457.2 s. Dry mass 6 t from Wikipedia. Fairing 2.6 t is an ASSUMPTION inside Beyond Gravity's 1.8-2.6 t range for the 20 m shell.
TIMELINE mode: ignition, cutoff, separation and fairing times are hard events. mdot = F_vac/(Isp_vac*g0). Full thrust; throttle unpublished.

cd.assumption: drag coefficient not published; same generic slender-launcher Cd used for Falcon 9 in this repo. Not fitted.
